Introduction

Clinical trials are research studies conducted involving human participants to evaluate new medical interventions such as drugs, devices, or procedures. Each clinical trial registered in the ClinicalTrials.gov database is assigned a unique National Clinical Trial (NCT) number. The NCT number NCT04421820 specifically refers to a registered clinical trial that can be accessed through this database for detailed information including the study's purpose, design, eligibility criteria, locations, and status. <Model name="Anthropic" version="claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219">

Clinical Trial Registration and Tracking

ClinicalTrials.gov serves as the official and comprehensive registry of clinical trials, maintained by the United States National Library of Medicine. This database contains information on clinical trials conducted not only in the United States but also in more than 200 other countries and territories across all disease areas and clinical development stages. <cite id="c69f4dd2-0"></cite>

When a clinical trial is registered, it is assigned a unique identifier—the National Clinical Trial (NCT) number. This NCT number functions as a specific reference point that can be used to download the full record of the study, making it easier for researchers, healthcare professionals, and the public to find and access detailed information about ongoing or completed trials. <cite id="c69f4dd2-0"></cite>

For COVID-19 vaccine trials specifically, researchers and tracking systems have leveraged these registries to monitor progress and results. One example is the regCOVID project, which expanded to track result articles generated from COVID-19 studies. This system identified 419 interventional trials and found 69 linked result articles for 40 vaccine trials (13.9% of 290 total COVID-19 vaccine trials), demonstrating how registration systems enable comprehensive tracking of clinical trial outcomes. <cite id="4dba0db1-0"></cite>

COVID-19 Vaccine Trial Information

The COVID-19 pandemic prompted an unprecedented global mobilization of clinical research, resulting in extensive registration of vaccine trials in databases like ClinicalTrials.gov. <cite id="4dba0db1-1">This registration process was recognized as a critical infrastructure for systematically identifying and monitoring all vaccine trials worldwide, regardless of their publication status, publication year, or language</cite>. <cite id="4dba0db1-2">Researchers developed specific search strategies across multiple registries including ClinicalTrials.gov, ISRCTN Register, the WHO vaccine trial website, and the Australia and New Zealand Clinical Trial Register to comprehensively identify vaccine trials conducted in various countries</cite>.

<cite id="4dba0db1-3">These databases became essential tools for tracking the progress and outcomes of vaccine trials, ensuring transparency about recruitment, results, and safety data</cite>. <cite id="4dba0db1-4">For example, comprehensive datasets of COVID-19-related clinical trials were compiled through Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov (AACT), which facilitated access to protocol and outcome data for all registered clinical trials</cite>. This extensive registration and tracking system proved invaluable for coordinating global vaccine development efforts, allowing stakeholders to monitor which trials were underway, their current status, and their findings as the pandemic evolved.

documents.snippet:
Our investigation of innovation responses to the COVID-19 crisis is based on a comprehensive dataset of clinical trials initiated between December 2019 and July 2020. We obtained the data via the Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov (AACT), provided by the Clinical Trial Transformation Initiative. 1 AACT facilitates access to the protocol and outcome data of all clinical trials registered in the ClinicalTrials. gov database, the official and comprehensive registry of clinical trials maintained by the United States National Library of Medicine. ClinicalTrials.gov contains information on clinical trials conducted in the United States and more than 200 other countries and territories across all disease areas and clinical development stages. Haeussler and Rake (2017) provide further details on the available information, the types of clinical trials registered, and the regulatory requirements related to trial registration in the ClinicalTrials.gov database. 2  In total, we identified 2,783 clinical trials related to COVID-19. The first clinical trials devoted to COVID-19 started on December 10, 2019, but we identified another 29 clinical trials that started before December 10, 2019, but were reclassified to address COVID-19 after the outbreak of the pandemic. While we included these reclassified clinical trials in our sample, we excluded 327 clinical trials that reported an (expected) start date after the end of July 2020 or did not report any start data, R&D Management 51, 4, 2021 397 because we wanted to focus on the realized clinical trials rather than intended future trials. This leaves us with a sample of 2,456 COVID-19-related clinical trials. 

Importantly, each clinical trial lists the sponsors associated with a given clinical trial. Sponsors are organizations (or individuals) that initiate, control, fund, or otherwise support the trial and are typically involved in both planning the trial and the analysis of the results. ClinicalTrials.gov provides only basic information about each clinical trials' lead-and cosponsors, which are referred to as 'collaborators' in the database. To gain deeper insights into the type and provenance of the individuals and organizations involved, we manually classified (co-)sponsors into different finer-grained categories based on publicly available information, such as the sponsors' websites.

Conclusion The Renal Lifecycle trial aims to investigate the effects of the SGLT2 inhibitor dapagliflozin compared with placebo on the incidence of kidney failure, heart failure, mortality and safety in three subgroups of patients with advanced CKD.

Title: Glomerular filtration rate as a kidney outcome of diabetic kidney disease: a focus on new antidiabetic drugs
Snippet: Diabetes has reached epidemic proportions, both in Korea and worldwide and is associated with an increased risk of chronic kidney disease and kidney failure (KF). The natural course of kidney function among people with diabetes (especially type 2 diabetes) may be complex in real-world situations. Strong evidence from observational data and clinical trials has demonstrated a consistent association between decreased estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and subsequent development of hard renal endpoints (such as KF or renal death). In addition, there are many patients with diabetes whose renal function declines without the appearance of albuminuria, measurement of the eGFR is emphasized. Snippet: We use descriptive statistics to present the number of patients at each DKD stage at the index date and DKD stage transition. Continuous variables, such as age, BMI, and laboratory values, are summarized using means and standard deviations. For the case count, we estimated the DKD cases each year and longitudinal changes in the number of patients across the years.
